chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abi Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of a female slave, so he said: Two divorces.
And he said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The waiting period of the female slave whose husband dies is two months and five days.
And the waiting period of the divorced female slave is one month and a half.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the distinct waiting periods for a female slave (ama), differentiating between the death of her husband (two months and five days) and divorce (one and a half months). This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic view that the 'iddah of a slave is half that of a free woman, derived from the Quranic verse on divorce, and highlights the specific legal status of concubines in early Islamic society.
